Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 3, Verse 35

“Better one's own duty imperfectly done than another's duty done well. Better death in one's own duty; another's duty brings danger.”

One of the Gita's most demanding verses. Krishna would rather Arjuna fail at his own life than succeed at a borrowed one — a standard that cuts against every instinct to imitate.
